source_obligations.statement: A finite voter carrier represents the district electorate; this is representation data for the source's finite voters.
A finite candidate carrier represents the candidates whose ballot rankings and STV tallies are used by the source rule.
Decidable equality on the finite voter carrier is an implementation representation of finite roster membership, not an added behavioral restriction.
Decidable equality on the finite candidate carrier is an implementation representation of finite roster membership, not an added electoral condition.
One finite voter roster represents the voters belonging to the Republican party in the two-party district.
One finite voter roster represents the voters belonging to the Democratic party in the two-party district.
One finite roster represents all voters in the district.
A ballot profile supplies the ranked ballots on which tallying, election, elimination, and transfer operate.
One finite candidate roster represents the Republican candidates.
One finite candidate roster represents the Democratic candidates.
The active candidate universe is the two named party rosters, recorded as source-model vocabulary rather than a hidden larger-candidate extension.
The district has a natural magnitude M, the number of seats in the displayed proposition.
The district has a natural voter count V used in its turnout and share conditions.
The real number y_R is the Republican share used in both the STV and PAV rounded-seat conclusions.
The STV rule ranges over a surplus-preserving ballot-routed transfer implementation, including the source's fractional and whole-vote examples.
The closeout records the approved positive-share convention 0<y_R; the zero-share branch is excluded rather than silently totalized.
A party fraction has the weak upper bound y_R<=1.
The displayed turnout condition is M(M+1)<=V.
There are at least M Republican candidates.
There are at least M Democratic candidates.
Republican voters rank every Republican candidate above every Democratic candidate.
Democratic voters rank every Democratic candidate above every Republican candidate.
The represented all-voter roster has cardinality V, connecting the finite model to the source turnout symbol.
The two party voter rosters exhaust the district electorate.
The two party voter rosters are disjoint, so each voter belongs to exactly one party.
The Republican and Democratic candidate rosters are disjoint.
Every Republican candidate is active at the start of the STV count.
Every Democratic candidate is active at the start of the STV count.
No extra active candidates occur beyond the two named party rosters; this records the source two-party active-candidate-universe convention.
The Republican roster size equals y_R times V in the real-share interpretation.
The Democratic roster size equals (1-y_R) times V in the real-share interpretation.

Proposition 1: in a two-party M-seat district with V >= M(M+1), at least M candidates per party, solid coalitions, and D-favoring ties, both the STV and PAV Republican seat counts are in {floor(y_R M), ceil(y_R M)}.
